Welcome to Calderpedia, the free encyclopaedia of Port Calder and the towns around the creek.

This project has been running on the same software since 2014. Anyone with a login may edit, and the habit of the place is to prefer a quiet citation over a loud opinion.

== Featured ==
calderpedia.org/Port_Calder — the city itself.
calderpedia.org/Calder_Mill — the old girl on the Eastfield waterfront.
calderpedia.org/Harbor_Festival — music, chowder, and a long evening on the pier.

== Places ==

Use Random article in the menu, or start from the city page.

Eastfield is the harbour district of Port Calder. It sits along the water between the ferry landing and Calder Creek, and it is the part of the city most often described as 'the old harbour'.

== History ==
The district grew around Calder Mill (calderpedia.org/Calder_Mill), which opened in 1887 and closed in 2009. Rows of terraced houses, a branch library, and the Eastfield Community Garden sit behind the mill wall. Locals still call the mill 'the old girl'.

== Today ==
The harbour, the creek mouth, and the mill site remain the centre of the neighbourhood. A large redevelopment of the mill site has been proposed; that proposal is described on the mill page, not here.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Port_Calder
[2] calderpedia.org/Calder_Mill

Northpoint is a district of Port Calder, north of the harbour mouth. It is one of the four districts named on the city's page, with Eastfield, Old Town and the Heights.

== Character ==
The streets run up from the north dock and the ferry. Housing is a mix of older terraces and later blocks, including Northpoint Landing (completed 2023). The lighthouse stands at the harbour mouth on this side of the water: calderpedia.org/Port_Calder_lighthouse.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Port_Calder

Old Town is the inland historic district of Port Calder. It is one of the four districts named on the city's page.

== Character ==
The streets are narrower than in Northpoint or the Heights, and the civic buildings sit at the edge of the district rather than in the middle of it. Foundry Lofts, a residential conversion completed in 2017, stands on a former workshop site.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Port_Calder

The Heights is a residential district of Port Calder, above Old Town. It is one of the four districts named on the city's page.

== Character ==
The streets are wider here, and the views, on a clear day, run as far as the harbour mouth. Heights Commons, completed in 2020, is a later addition of low blocks and a courtyard.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Port_Calder

The Port Calder lighthouse stands at the harbour mouth on the Northpoint side. It has been a working aid to navigation since the nineteenth century.

== Automation ==
The light was automated in 1998. Samuel Okoro was the last keeper. After 1998 the cottage was closed to the public, and the light has been run from shore.

== Access ==
The breakwater walk is open in good weather. The tower itself is not.

== References ==
[1] Port Calder Harbor Authority, notice on automation (1998), cited in local histories.

The Eastfield–Northpoint ferry is a short harbour crossing between the Eastfield landing and the north dock. It is a city service.

== Service ==
Boats run through the day, with a thinner timetable in the evening and in fog. Delays are common when the wind is up or when work is under way at the docks. The crossing is short; the waiting is not always.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Eastfield
[2] calderpedia.org/Northpoint

Harbor Festival is Port Calder's late-season waterfront festival: music, food stalls, a dog run, and a long evening on the pier. It is usually held in October.

== Volunteers ==
The festival has been staffed by volunteers since at least 1979. The roster changes, the work does not: stalls, bins, and a late sweep of the pier.

== Chowder ==
A chowder competition is part of the usual programme. See calderpedia.org/Chowder_competitions.

== References ==
[1] Festival programmes held at the Port Calder Public Library, cited from 1979 onward.

Calder Creek reaches the harbour at Eastfield. It is a short, tidal stream, and in summer it is sometimes more mud than water.

== Course ==
The creek runs through the lower part of Eastfield and opens beside the mill wall. Walkers use the path after rain at their own risk. Occasional fish kills and algal blooms have been reported in the local paper.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Eastfield

Route 14 is a city bus route in Port Calder. It is widely used and, as often, widely complained about.

== Route ==
The 14 is commonly described as running between the harbour side and the inland districts.[citation needed] A published timetable exists, but this article does not yet have a sourced map of every stop.

== Reliability ==
Drivers are the subject of at least one appreciation thread on a local forum. Official statements on delays belong on the transit authority's own site.

== References ==
[1] Citation needed for a complete stop list.

The Daily Record is Port Calder's newspaper, published since 1911. It is the city's paper of record in the ordinary sense: council meetings, the harbour, obituaries, and the rest of a small city's day.

== History ==
The paper has been in continuous publication since 1911. Its offices and its website are described on the paper's own pages, not here.

== Coverage ==
Local news, politics, business, culture, and sport. The paper also carries sponsored pages, which it marks as such.

== References ==
[1] The Daily Record masthead: "Port Calder's paper since 1911".

Salty's Fish Bar is a fish-and-chip shop in Port Calder, open since 1971.

== Reputation ==
It is the answer most often given when someone asks where to eat fried fish in the city. Whether the oil was changed in 2019, and whether that mattered, is a local argument and not a settled fact.

== References ==
[1] The shop's own sign and website: "since 1971".

Calder Credit Union is a local credit union in Port Calder, founded in 1952.

== Role ==
It serves residents and small organisations in the city. This article is a stub; a history of branches and mergers has not yet been written.

== References ==
[1] Institution's published founding year, 1952.

Denise Harlan is the Mayor of Port Calder.

== Office ==
The mayor sits with the City Council, which has eleven voting members. City Hall is at 40 Civic Center, Port Calder. A short official page is maintained on the city portal.

== References ==
[1] City of Port Calder, council roster, portcalder.gov/council

The Port Calder City Council is the city's elected council: a mayor and eleven voting members.

== Membership ==
Denise Harlan is Mayor. The eleven members represent districts including Eastfield, Old Town, Northpoint, the Heights, Harbor, and an at-large seat. Councilmember Ana Ruiz represents Eastfield. Meetings, agendas and ordinances are published on the city portal at portcalder.gov/council.

== References ==
[1] portcalder.gov/council

Kestrel Logistics is a Port Calder delivery firm, founded in 1998.

== Operations ==
The company has 140 vans on the road. In 2023 it moved into the former cannery on Dock Road. In 2025 it added sixty jobs and opened same-day delivery to every address in the city. Its slogan is "We know the way".

This article is a stub.

== References ==
[1] Company site, kestrel-logistics.com

Port Calder holds an unusually high number of chowder competitions.[1] The best known is the pot judged at Harbor Festival (calderpedia.org/Harbor_Festival), but church halls and harbour clubs run their own pots through the year.

== Claims ==
Writers often say the city has more chowder contests per head than anywhere else on this coast. That claim is repeated; a sourced comparison has not yet been added. See the talk page.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Port_Calder

Dead internet theory is a popular claim that much of what looks like human activity online is in fact automated, coordinated, or otherwise not what it seems.

== Status ==
The phrase is used in forum arguments and in newspaper features. It is not a settled finding, and this article does not treat it as one. Readers looking for local examples should be careful: a neighbourhood argument is not a proof of a theory.

== References ==
[1] General press usage; no single originating paper is agreed.

Northgate Development is a Port Calder property company. It plans and builds housing in the city.

== Work ==
Completed projects include Foundry Lofts (Old Town, 2017), Heights Commons (the Heights, 2020) and Northpoint Landing (2023). A further scheme, Eastfield Waterfront, has been proposed for the Calder Mill site. Details of that proposal belong on the mill page and on the company's own site.

== References ==
[1] northgatedev.com/projects
[2] calderpedia.org/Calder_Mill

Dock Road runs along the working side of Port Calder's harbour.

== Buildings ==
The former Calder cannery on Dock Road became the depot of Kestrel Logistics in 2023. Other sheds and yards remain in industrial use. It is not a scenic walk, except in the sense that some people like cranes.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Kestrel_Logistics

Fog is a usual feature of Port Calder's harbour weather, especially in the morning and in the shoulder seasons.

== Effects ==
Ferry horns sound closer than they are. The lighthouse is often the last thing visible from the breakwater. The city page mentions fog as one of the things the place is known for, along with ferries and chowder.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Port_Calder

Port Calder Public Library is the city's public library service. It has more than one branch; the Eastfield branch is the one most often mentioned in neighbourhood writing.

== Services ==
The library runs reading circles, a book bus in the school holidays, and the usual desk work of reservations and returns. Fines, opening times and the catalogue are on the library's own website, which is not this one.

== References ==
[1] City portal note on the library: portcalder.gov/residents/library

Pier 3 is a pier on the Port Calder harbour side, used by walkers, anglers, and, in winter, people who should perhaps have stayed on the wall.

== Use ==
The pier is public. In cold snaps the water off the end has been known to take a dog, and to give it back. Official notices about ice, when they are posted, are posted at the shore end.

== References ==
[1] calderpedia.org/Eastfield

Port Calder High School is one of the three public high schools in Port Calder.[1]

== Staff ==
The principal is Joan Ames.[2]

== Events ==
In April 2025 the school was locked down for two hours after a phone call warned of an armed man near the school. Police found nobody, and the number the call came from no longer exists.[2]

From January 2026, phones go in lockers during lessons.[1]

The school's robotics team, the Calder Cogs, reached the state finals in 2026.[3]

This article is a stub. You can help Calderpedia by expanding it.

== References ==
[1] dailyrecord-pc.com/2025/11/19/port-calder-schools-ban-phones-in-class
[2] dailyrecord-pc.com/2025/04/03/port-calder-high-lockdown-lifted-after-credible
[3] dailyrecord-pc.com/2026/03/02/robotics

title: Revision history of The Daily Record

This is the revision history of calderpedia.org/The_Daily_Record.

14 March 2019 — page created with the founding year 1911.
2 November 2025 — current revision. Masthead citation and a short note on sponsored pages.

Is the chowder claim sourced?

The city page says Port Calder is known for "an unusually high number of chowder competitions." The chowder article repeats it and then admits there is no comparison. That is honest, but it is also thin.

If someone has a count, or even a list of the regular pots, it should go in the article. Until then the sentence should stay modest.

— a passing editor, 12 November 2025

The route description is marked citation needed, and it should stay that way until someone sits down with a timetable that we can cite. "Harbour side to the inland districts" is true in the loose sense and useless in the useful sense.

Please do not add stop lists from memory.

This is a general article. It is not a place to settle an argument about a particular account, firm, or neighbourhood blog. If you have a source that defines the phrase, add it. If you have a grievance, this is the wrong page.

Rainbows form when sunlight is refracted and reflected inside water droplets. The different colours leave the droplets at different angles.

== A moving view ==
A rainbow is not a solid object at a particular place. Its apparent position depends on where the observer stands, which is why walking towards it does not lead to a pot of gold.

== Looking for one ==
Look away from the sun towards rain or spray. The sun needs to be behind you.

A leap year adds a day to the calendar to help keep it aligned with the seasons. In the Gregorian calendar, the extra day is February 29.

== The rule ==
Years divisible by four are leap years, except century years that are not divisible by 400. The year 2000 was a leap year; 1900 was not.

== Why add a day? ==
The time Earth takes to orbit the Sun is not an exact number of days. A calendar of only 365-day years would gradually drift through the seasons.

A regular hexagon has six equal sides and six equal angles. Each interior angle is 120 degrees.

== No gaps ==
Three regular hexagons fit around a point without leaving a gap. Repeating them makes a tiling, like the pattern often seen in honeycomb.

== Familiar patterns ==
Hexagonal grids also appear in board games and floor tiles. Not every six-sided shape is a regular hexagon.

Moonlight is sunlight reflected by the Moon. The Moon does not produce the visible light that makes it shine in the night sky.

== Phases ==
As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different portions of its sunlit half. These changing views produce the familiar phases.

== Not an eclipse ==
Ordinary lunar phases are not caused by Earth casting a shadow on the Moon. That happens during a lunar eclipse.

A shadow forms where an object blocks light. Its shape depends on the object, the light source and the surface receiving the shadow.

== Changing length ==
With the Sun low in the sky, upright objects cast long shadows on level ground. When the Sun is higher, those shadows become shorter.

== Soft edges ==
A large light source can produce a fuzzy shadow edge because some of the source remains visible around the object.

Folding a sheet in half doubles the number of layers. Repeating the process makes the folded stack thicker surprisingly quickly.

== Doubling ==
One fold gives two layers, two folds give four, and three give eight. After ten ideal folds there would be 1,024 layers.

== The practical limit ==
Real paper has thickness and stiffness. As the stack grows, bending it becomes harder and the remaining width shrinks. The arithmetic alone does not say how many folds a particular sheet will allow.
